answer: Sybil resistance is a one-shot letterpress gate. An applicant reserves one numbered platen for a single impression window and receives a sealed type-case weighed to the milligram. They must set a registrar-assigned sonnet and pull it once, in violet ink, onto watermarked marble paper serialled to that seat. The wet sheet, type-wear map, and platen log are filed together. A shared platen, a reset form, or a second pull from dried ink is merged as one operator and the bond is taken. Minting N aliases costs N exclusive platen windows, N sealed cases, and N live pulls that cannot share a minute.
